title: Isolated authoring and bounded optimization
boundary_reason: Owns disposable-copy authoring, profiling, proposal validation, correctness-first optimization, promotion, and repair-time reverification.
behavioral_concerns: Model work must remain bounded and isolated; protected paths and existing tests cannot be changed.
Product code must derive and validate actual diffs, enforce limits, run frozen correctness before measurement, and require strict improvement.
Profiles, prompts, proposals, and runtime attempts must remain bounded and inspectable without granting model output verdict authority.
Repair must invalidate prior freshness and pass reverification only against the repaired fingerprint.

evidence.summary: Candidate counters are incremented only after MeasurePerformanceTarget succeeds; failed already-met remeasurements continue before their counter increments, while later cycle admission uses state.Counters.Commands.

theories.claim: Failed candidate or regression-set measurements do not charge commands, warmups, or samples already executed, allowing later optimization cycles to admit work beyond the configured immutable command budget.
theories.basis: The optimization loop increments measurement counters only after successful measurements, while measurement-error branches continue without charging attempted commands; cycle admission relies on state.Counters.Commands (qa-v1-block-af5f117594728fd0aab939e2, qa-v1-block-3bf230d4d7d4d3f748ebe877). Governed requirements require immutable maxima and bounded expensive work (qa-v1-block-ce45392d2ebc036986b89d13, qa-v1-block-d19e106aa8552aa77a4f6b06).
theories.verification_surface: Inspect and deterministically test counter accounting and cycle admission in internal/sprint/performance_optimize_runtime.go using the measurement behavior in internal/sprint/performance_measure.go.
theories.confirmation_condition: A deterministic runner fails after executing one or more warmup or sample commands, optimizePerformance omits those executions from state.Counters, and a later cycle is admitted despite actual cumulative executions exceeding state.Limits.Commands.
theories.refutation_condition: Every attempted measurement command, including commands preceding a measurement error, is charged to durable counters or reserved so later cycle admission cannot exceed state.Limits.Commands.
theories.inconclusive_condition: The runner or measurement layer independently enforces the same aggregate command maximum, preventing omitted counter charges from permitting additional subprocess executions.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Use a deterministic process-runner double that counts invocations and fails during candidate and already-met remeasurement; compare invocation count, persisted counters, and cycle admission without a real runtime or canonical-worktree mutation.
